title: Today's musicians study; Eubie Blake on reading
summary: Young musicians are better trained; Johnston relays Eubie Blake's story about the myth that Black musicians couldn't read.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Oh it's impossible to almost play if you can't read today. Isn't it, yes?

Well, they have the, fortunately they have the, we have talked about this for years. And they get the knowledge from us that the smartest thing to do is study and practice. And learn all your harmonies and where it is on your instrument. And if you play a different instrument, naturally piano has to know them all, or bass or guitar or (braphones), they have to know all their harmonies. But your horn blowers they've got to study that harmony to know where it is on their instruments so they have facility to

Your saying that you don't look at, don't use music today reminds me of a story that Eubie Blake tells me. And he said that it was unthinkable at least I'll put it this way. That white people simply didn't think that negroes could read music at all. And so they used to have to get the show tunes and whatever else it was because you see these negro musicians as you know, used to play for these rich white people in their homes. The Jim Europe bands that were sent out.

And he said they would get the music and learn all the scores you see and then they would get before these white people and play. And the white people would stand around and say, aren't they fantastic? And they can't even read. (LAUGHTER).
Well they didn't know. They didn't know.
